summary: Frontend-only testing of the mobile scroll-snap fix on the homepage (/). Verified via Playwright on three criteria: (1) mobile 375px viewport has snap disabled (free scroll), (2) desktop 1440px viewport retains y-mandatory snap, (3) homepage loads with all sections visible and zero JS errors.

1_mobile_snap_disabled.free_scroll_test: scrollBy(0,300) -> scrollTop=300 (no jump, landed exactly at 300px)
1_mobile_snap_disabled.notes: CSS @media (max-width:1024px) rule correctly sets scroll-snap-type:none on .brief-page and scroll-snap-align:none on all direct section/footer children. Free scrolling confirmed.

2_desktop_snap_active.snap_test: scrollBy(0,100) -> scrollTop settled at 788px (= exact section height, correctly snapped to section 2)
2_desktop_snap_active.notes: Desktop snap-scroll works correctly — 100px nudge triggers full snap to next section (788px). Footer retains end-align and always-stop.

3_sections_and_errors.notes: 10 sections + 1 footer rendered inside .brief-page. No JS console errors.

critical_code_review_comments: CSS fix is correct and minimal: @media (max-width:1024px) sets scroll-snap-type:none on .brief-page and scroll-snap-align:none + scroll-snap-stop:unset on .brief-page > section and .brief-page > footer. No regressions on desktop.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Homepage scroll-snap fix verified. Mobile 375px: scroll-snap-type=none (free scroll confirmed). Desktop 1440px: scroll-snap-type=y mandatory, sections snap correctly. 10 sections + footer present. 0 JS errors.
rca of the issue: Root cause: CSS scroll-snap-type:y mandatory with scroll-snap-stop:always on .brief-page > section forces a snap on every touchmove event. On mobile, sections are taller than the viewport so the first touch-scroll immediately triggers snap to the next section before the user can read current content. Fix: @media (max-width:1024px) disables all snap properties, restoring native free scroll on mobile. Desktop behavior (snap section-by-section) is unchanged.
